commits.summary: Add symbolic, capability and TLA+ verification examples 006 to 012
Credit example authors and commit the TLA+ standard modules
Reword the note on which examples to read first
Add hand-written session notes to the trace summaries
Link the blog post now that it is on GitHub
Generate a traces overview at llm-dlc/traces/README.md
Run the trace pipeline on commit and push, not on every turn
Correct the definition of session status

prompts.text: This POC code shows examples of how to leverage LLMs to formally verify existing software (see `./examples` folder.) The current examples are somewhat trivial, in the sense that adding a type system…
[Request interrupted by user for tool use]

Add a comment to the top of examples/README.md indicating that the first 5 examples were created by Opus 5.5, and examples 6-12 were created by Fable 5.1. Encourage the user to look at the Fable exam…
I made a small change to examples README wording. Do a final sanity check, then commit my changes and push to remote. Note: one of the traces describes a session done outside of this codebase, where…

I've pushed the blog to the Terminal-Value repo adjacent to this repo's remote. You can update the link to it now, then commit and push all uncommitted changes. Leave the repository in a clean state,…
Add a more comprehensive summary of traces to the `./llm-dlc/traces` folder as a README, integrated with the toolchain.
The current way of commiting traces (stop hook) is a bit clunky as it leaves commits without traces. The trace pipeline should be initiated on commit as well. Also, in this situation we are ready to…
